recipes.name: Chipotle and Adobo Pickled Eggs
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon adobo sauce from canned chipotle peppers

steps.text: In a large pot, combine the vinegar, water, garlic, onion, salt, sugar, chipotle chiles and adobo sauce. Bring to a boil, and cook until the onion is translucent, about 15 minutes.

Place the hard-cooked eggs into clean jars. Strain the boiling brine into the jars to cover the eggs. Cover with lids and refrigerate for at least 3 days before serving. Store in the refrigerator for up to 6 weeks.

raw_recipe.headline: Chipotle and Adobo Pickled Eggs
raw_recipe.description: These pickled eggs are great sliced and served on a salad or just eat them plain for a quick low carb snack! You can adjust the heat by adding more or less chipotle and adobo.

review.reviewBody: actually just a question...is it two peppers from a can of chipotles or two whole cans of chipotles?

I have made it and do enjoy it but very little chipotle flavor. I would suggest to put the pepper in the jar split open instead of the sauce pan and add another two spoonfuls of the Adobe sauce into the sauce pan. this should give you a better result.

This is a great recipe! I have made this a couple of times. I like to make a large batch in a 2quart jar and add the entire can of chipotles. Also they are best after about three months in the fridge.
OMG!! These were a big hit with my family! The only thing I changed was that I did NOT stain the brine. I left the onion, garlic and ONE pepper in the jar. Thanks!
loves these for snacking! Doubled the peppers and added a few tablespoons of sugar for a more sweet heat Chipotle flavor. Excellent!

Fantastic recipe. I will make again, but make it a little more spicy. In my first batch, I used large eggs and only a single quart jar, so I only got 9 or 10 eggs in there. Because I knew the liquid would be too much for one jar, and because I love the vinegar flavor, I cut the water in half. I still had too much and should cut it further. I used the recipe amount of peppers, onions and garlic. I would like it spicier next time, so I would probably double the peppers. Thank you for a great recipe.
I added garlic cloves, mushrooms, and precooked sausages. Makes a great snack!

Fantastic Results. 1/2 can(it's a small can to begin with) of Chipotles & adobo sauce. Put eggs in pot, brought water to boil over medium heat,then timed 17-18 mins, eggs into cold water until cool/cold before shelling - worked for me. It's a Keeper!
Overall, pretty good. I was expecting a little more "kick" since I doubled the chipotle. But the flavor was nice.

I just made these. The recipe calls for a lot of brine if you are using jars. I filled a quart jar with 12 eggs and still had more than half of the brine left. So I made a 2nd dozen eggs in another quart jar, and still had brine left over. To be fair though, I didn't see the step saying to strain the brine, so I packed a couple of the onions and peppers in there too.
They taste like a plain pickled egg. But... The onions are great! I used those by themselves and made some more to have. Great pickled onion recipe.
I had some frozen adobe chilis and for 8 eggs, I used 1 chili and it added plenty of spice for me.

Delicious eggs that go with everything. I added extra chipotles because we like things hot but we still found them to be mild albeit full of flavor. That smoky taste is so unique and that's what sets these apart from your regular pickled eggs. Thank you for the recipe.
great recipe, eggs are smokey in flavor, awesome

I made these exactly as written. I wasn't a fan. I love spicy food and I love pickled eggs so I thought this would be a match made in heaven. I was completely wrong. There didn't seem to be very much flavor. I'll go back to making pickled eggs the way I usually do and maybe adding in some crushed red pepper and cayenne.
I absolutely love this recipe! Has heat and lots of flavor. Instead of a cookie .. go for these eggs. They are filling and yummy. Thank you for such a great idea.

I loved the change of pace from the usual pickled egg. That said, these aren't spicy at all, for those who are scared to try them. On the heat scale, they were about a 1. I ended up adding 2 whole peppers into the jar and that took them to about a 3-4 on the spicy scale. Be sure to strain the brine or else you will get a lot of sediment in your jar.
Was very easy, but not a very strong flavor .will make these again ,but will add more chipotle,onions, and garlic.
